riskTone.label: BULLISH
riskTone.rationale: Cool US inflation data and solid bank earnings drove equity gains; mild risk from US-Iran tension and gold safe-haven demand limit full risk-on.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture first — GBPUSD is up +0.32% today, sitting at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range (meaning sterling is unusually strong right now), and because UK100 and sterling move in OPPOSITE directions (most FTSE 100 companies earn in dollars and euros, so a weaker pound makes those overseas earnings worth more when converted back), the snapshot rates this GBP move as NEUTRAL for the index rather than a meaningful tailwind — it's not a big enough move to flip the index sharply either way. The dominant forces today are clearly the commodity sectors: Brent crude is up a strong +2.85%, which is directly bullish for Shell and BP (top-5 index weights), and copper is up +1.5%, which lifts the miners — Rio, Glencore, Anglo, and Antofagasta — acting as a positive signal for global growth and Chinese demand; both sectors are rated BULLISH. Gilts (UK government bonds) are calm — the 10-year yield is down just 2 basis points (a tiny move), long-end stress is absent, and banks are NEUTRAL. The key catalyst came roughly 1 hour ago: Reuters reported that the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed higher on cooler-than-expected US inflation data and solid US bank earnings — this is the single biggest story driving markets right now, explaining the bullish risk tone and commodity strength. Pharma remains idiosyncratic, meaning AstraZeneca could move the index independently on any stock-specific news. The overall directional bias leans BULLISH, driven by the commodity one-two punch and the positive US lead, though a slightly stronger pound and crowded short positioning in GBP (which is a contrarian bearish signal for the index via the sign-flip) prevent a higher conviction score — confidence sits at 5/10, and the view would weaken if sterling strengthens further or oil gives back today's gains, and would strengthen if tomorrow morning sees follow-through buying in miners and energy names. For the 08:00 ORB trade specifically, today's context is challenging: the ORB has already broken to the DOWNSIDE (the price already moved below the opening range low of 10,447.4), and critically the 14-day average daily range has already been used 104% — meaning the market has already moved more than a typical full day's range, which dramatically reduces the probability of a clean, trending breakout and raises the risk of chop or mean-reversion; this is a STAND-ASIDE or extreme-caution day for new ORB entries. No UK data is scheduled for today, but there is a HIGH-impact event already behind us — US CPI at 13:30 BST — and traders should build in caution ahead of the UK GDP Monthly Estimate due Thursday at 07:00 BST (two days away), which lands just before the London cash open and could gap the index sharply. Key levels to watch: overnight high 10,499.9 and prior day high 10,526.3 as resistance above; overnight low 10,414.8 and the ORB low 10,447.4 as the key support/breakdown zone below; current price is 10,479.1, sitting in the middle of this range. The market has already run its average daily range — respect the boundaries and wait for a fresh session to reset.
